Q. 1 زَغْرَدَةٌ The braying that is reiterated (L, K) in the fauces, or throat, (L,) or in the جَوْف [meaning chest], (K,) of the camel: (L, K:) an inf. n., of which the verb is زَغْرَدَ: you say, زَغْرَدَ البَعِيرُ. (TK.) ―
-b2- Hence the زَغْرَدَة of women on the occasions of rejoicings. (TA.) [One says, of a woman, زَغْرَدَتْ, more commonly in the present day زَغْرَطَتْ, meaning She uttered shrill, quavering, or rapidly-reiterated, sounds, or cries of joy: which sounds, or cries, are termed ↓ زَغَارِيدُ , and now more commonly زَغَارِيط.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
